definitions.gloss: hand-me-down; something used and passed on
definitions.explanation: Things, especially clothes, that someone else has used and then passed on.

examples.english: I wear my older sister's hand-me-downs.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→自転車：00633_jitensha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{兄|あに}→兄：00570_ani⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{古|ふる}だ。
examples.english: This bicycle is a hand-me-down from my older brother.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{古|ふる}⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧で、⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なかった→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: As a child I only got hand-me-downs and was never bought new clothes.

notes:
Usually said with the person it came from: ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{古|ふる} (my sister's hand-me-downs).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{古|ふる}: ~'s hand-me-downs
- お{古|ふる}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧: to get hand-me-downs
- お{古|ふる}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧: to wear hand-me-downs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{下|さ}がり: hand-me-downs from an older sibling or a superior (the most common word for clothes passed down in a family)
- ⟦{中古|ちゅうこ}→中古：03479_chuuko⟧: secondhand goods that are bought and sold (cars, books)
